description: Three distinct accounts now exist of the 20 May 2025 council meeting. (1) Seven of the original eight source documents, and the independently-fetched Macleay Argus (EV-0001), describe council declining the management-plan request outright on budget grounds, with a separate informal hope to revisit in October. (2) The Hardened Submission Package (EV-0010) describes a specific numbered sequence - Resolution 2025.79, a 2/7-defeated amendment, and Resolution 2025.80 passed 9/0 directing investigation and an October report-back. (3) Operator-relayed research (EV-0014, 2026-08-23) describes an unanimous resolution to hold a meeting, investigate management options, and report back - consistent in substance with (2) but without the specific resolution numbers or vote count, and consistent with what actually followed (the August 2025 meeting and September 2025 door-knocking read more naturally as fulfilling a resolution to investigate than as unprompted goodwill after a flat decline).
material_significance: Determines the actual statutory weight of council's October failure. With EV-0014, the balance of evidence now leans toward council having passed *some* affirmative resolution to investigate and report back, not merely declining and hoping to revisit - narrowing the live dispute to whether the specific resolution numbers, 9/0 vote count, and defeated 2/7 amendment in EV-0010 are accurate, which remains unconfirmed and is the load-bearing claim for the Hardened Submission Package's SafeWork NSW and Office of Local Government submissions.
required_resolution: The signed confirmed minutes of the 20 May 2025 Kempsey Shire Council ordinary meeting, read directly rather than via search snippet or press summary. The council's own site and web.archive.org both blocked automated fetch attempts on 2026-08-22 and 2026-08-23; this requires either a manual browser fetch of the meeting-minutes PDF or a GIPA/formal records request.

description: Council's current flying-fox page reportedly lists Bellbrook as a 'historic flying-fox camp' (EV-0016, partially corroborated). A June 2026 report reportedly describes the camp as severely affecting residents, with the park unusable, waste affecting public areas, impacts on Bellbrook Public School children, and residents still seeking intervention (EV-0015, not yet independently located). If both hold up, Council's own published classification does not match the functional reality described contemporaneously. This is complicated by EV-0013 (independently found): Council's own 27 October 2021 page reports the colony left Bellbrook that year - meaning 'historic' may accurately describe an earlier departure rather than being a stale or inaccurate label for a camp that never left.
material_significance: If confirmed as described, this would be the case's clearest single instance of the Documented Compliance vs. Functional Compliance pattern - a formal classification that doesn't match the situation on the ground. But it is not yet confirmed: the June 2026 report has not been located by this repository, and EV-0013 shows a real, independently-documented departure in 2021 that could fully explain the classification without any inaccuracy on Council's part - the open question is whether the colony returned after 2021, not whether Council's page is wrong.
required_resolution: Direct sighting of the June 2026 report (citation needed from operator - see Q-0009), and confirmation of whether the colony that prompted the case's 2025-2026 material is a return of the same or a new colony after the 2021 departure, or whether the 2021 departure was brief/partial and the case's 'continuous since 2019' framing needs revision instead.
